rules.statement: When the customer a gift card is assigned to is deleted, the card must not become spendable by anyone again (it keeps a trace of the assignment and stays restricted/locked until staff reassign it).

signature.follows: every user-deleting path calls giftcard.utils.deactivate_assigned_gift_cards(users) inside the deletion transaction before user.delete(); it keeps assigned_to_email and sets is_active=False. GiftCard.assigned_to is on_delete=PROTECT (models.py:74). grep: deactivate_assigned_gift_cards
signature.breaks: a path that deletes users (User.objects...delete(), instance.delete(), queryset.delete()) without that call; or changing assigned_to to on_delete SET_NULL/CASCADE; or clearing assigned_to_email / leaving is_active=True when detaching. grep: '\.delete\(\)' on User querysets with no deactivate_assigned_gift_cards nearby. NOTE: the code deactivates the card rather than keeping it active-but-restricted; the follow signature is that, not literal 'restricted'.

consistent.ticket: Add a 'deleteInactiveCustomers' bulk mutation that deletes all customers with no orders and no login for N months.
consistent.rule_test: Create a customer, assign an active restricted gift card to them, run the mutation, then assert the card still exists, is not active (not spendable) and still carries assigned_to_email; the deletion must not raise ProtectedError.

none.ticket: Add a scheduled task in saleor/account/tasks.py that deletes customer accounts flagged by a new 'delete_requested_at' older than 30 days (GDPR erasure).
none.rule_test: Same as consistent: assigned active card is not spendable by anyone after the task deletes its assignee, and the task does not crash on PROTECT.

contradicting.ticket: Add a 'deleteInactiveCustomers' bulk mutation that deletes all customers with no orders and no login for N months.
contradicting.rule_test: Same as consistent site; a violation shows as ProtectedError, or as an assigned card that is still active/spendable after deletion.
contradicting.seeding: Remove the deactivate_assigned_gift_cards call (+ import) from customer_bulk_delete, staff_bulk_delete and customer_delete (~9 lines). 3 of 5 precedents then break (60%). Caveat: with PROTECT in place those deletes now raise ProtectedError when a card is assigned, so the seed also needs a 'quiet break' variant to be realistic: leave the calls but change assigned_to to on_delete=SET_NULL (1 line in giftcard/models.py + migration), which breaks the rule for all 5 at once. Tests that would fail: saleor/graphql/giftcard/tests/test_user_delete_deactivates_assigned_cards.py (and any account bulk-delete/customer-delete tests with an assigned card; none found by name beyond that file).

rules.neutral_patch: In saleor/graphql/account, extract the 'deactivate_assigned_gift_cards + delete_user_unique_attribute_values' pair into one helper (e.g. giftcard.utils or account.utils 'prepare_users_for_deletion') and call it from the same 5 places (~15 lines); every precedent still follows.
rules.why: Natural consistent site (5/5) and natural none site exist; contradicting needs a small seed. Rule is only visible to a behaviour test (deletion then assert card not spendable), and PROTECT makes naive violations fail loudly, so the 'break' needs the SET_NULL variant.

rules.statement: webhookUpdate/webhookDelete accept `identifier` as an alternative to `id` only from an app referencing its own webhook; staff must use `id`, and no `app` argument is added without revisiting the decision.

signature.follows: pointers resolved through resolve_webhook_id-style helper in saleor/graphql/webhook/mutations/utils.py that rejects identifier when app is None and looks up app.webhooks.filter(identifier=...). grep: 'identifier=' in saleor/graphql/webhook/mutations
signature.breaks: accepting identifier from staff (no app), adding an `app` argument to webhook mutations, or looking up Webhook by identifier globally (Webhook.objects.filter(identifier=...) without app scope).

consistent.ticket: Let an app (or staff user) pass a webhook's identifier to a new 'webhookEnable/webhookDisable' mutation instead of the global id.
consistent.rule_test: Call the new mutation with identifier as a staff user: must be rejected with an identifier error; as an app with its own webhook identifier: succeeds; identifier of another app's webhook: not resolved.

none.package: saleor/graphql/app/mutations (identifier exists for apps, but no webhook-pointer precedent)
none.ticket: Let an app (or staff user) pass a webhook's identifier to a new 'appWebhookSetActive' mutation under the app mutations instead of the global id.

contradicting.ticket: Let an app (or staff user) pass a webhook's identifier to a new 'webhookEnable/webhookDisable' mutation instead of the global id.
contradicting.seeding: Only 3 precedents exist, so flip 2 of 3 (67%): make the shared helper accept identifier without an app (global lookup) and give webhookUpdate an `app` arg (~15-25 lines). Tests that fail: saleor/graphql/webhook/tests for webhookUpdate/webhookDelete identifier-by-staff rejection cases. The seed necessarily rewrites the ADR-protected helper itself, so the 'precedent' is the rule's own implementation.

rules.neutral_patch: Rename the helper and move it to saleor/graphql/webhook/utils.py (or inline docstring/arg-order refactor, ~10 lines) with unchanged behaviour.
rules.why: One narrow decision with 3 precedents all in one tiny package; the contradicting condition means breaking the rule's own enforcement point, and the 'none' site is a contrived mutation with nothing to imitate. A ticket that naturally invites the violation (identifier for staff) is easy to spot.

rules.statement: Resolve the current site with Site.objects.get_current() or the get_site_promise dataloader, never by reading settings.SITE_ID or assuming a single Site row.

signature.follows: get_site_promise(info.context).get() in the GraphQL layer; Site.objects.get_current() elsewhere.
signature.breaks: settings.SITE_ID, Site.objects.get(pk=settings.SITE_ID), Site.objects.get() / .first() with no resolved site, per-site cache keys/module dicts using a constant. grep: 'SITE_ID|Site\.objects\.(get|first)\('

consistent.ticket: Add a shop setting 'checkoutNoteMaxLength' that an admin can update and the storefront can read.
consistent.rule_test: Run the new mutation/resolver with settings.SITE_ID unset (or pointing at another Site) and two Site rows with different Host; assert the setting is read/written on the Site matching the request host, not Site #SITE_ID or the first row.

none.ticket: Add a shop setting 'defaultGiftCardNote' that the giftCardCreate mutation uses when no note is given, plus an admin mutation to update it.
none.rule_test: Same multi-site assertion: two Sites, SITE_ID unset or pointing at the other; the default is taken from the request's Site.

contradicting.ticket: Add a shop setting 'lowStockWarningThreshold' that bulk stock mutations use to report variants dropping below it.
contradicting.rule_test: Same multi-site assertion: with two Sites and differing settings, the threshold used by the bulk stock mutation is the request Site's.
contradicting.seeding: In product_variant_stocks_create and _update replace get_site_promise(info.context).get().settings with Site.objects.get(pk=settings.SITE_ID).settings (+ import settings/Site; ~4 lines each, ~8 total). 2 of 3 precedents break (67%). Only 3 precedents exist in the package, so the margin is thin. Tests that would fail: probably none (test settings define SITE_ID); a multi-site test must be added to expose it. Natural contradicting package does not exist: the only SITE_ID reads are the resolvers themselves (saleor/graphql/site/dataloaders.py:36-37, saleor/site/patch_sites.py:24-25), which are correct fallbacks.

rules.neutral_patch: In saleor/graphql/shop, hoist the repeated 'site = get_site_promise(info.context).get()' into one helper in shop/utils.py and call it from the 9 places (~20 lines); all still follow.
rules.why: Clean regex-visible signature, natural consistent (9/9) and none sites; no natural contradicting site because the repo is uniformly compliant, so one small seed is required.

rules.source: AGENTS.md (architecture: do not use Django signals)
rules.statement: Do not use Django signals (post_save, pre_delete, @receiver); call the logic explicitly from the code that triggers it (post_migrate for data-migration tasks is the only exception).

signature.follows: side effect of a save/delete invoked explicitly from the mutation/service that triggers it (e.g. deactivate_assigned_gift_cards(...) and delete_user_unique_attribute_values(...) before user.delete(); delete_files_from_private_storage_task.delay(...) in app/tasks.py:82). Fuzzy: there is no single follow token.
signature.breaks: grep: '@receiver|\.connect\(|from django.db.models.signals|from django.dispatch'; handlers registered in apps.py ready().

consistent.ticket: When a customer is deleted, also remove their uploaded avatar file and queued export files immediately.
consistent.rule_test: Static check on the diff/tree: no new '@receiver', '.connect(' or 'django.db.models.signals' import outside saleor/permission/apps.py (post_migrate) and the existing allowlist; optionally assert delete mutation triggers the cleanup task with a mock.

none.ticket: When a gift card is deleted, also cancel its scheduled expiry-reminder tasks and remove its search-index entry immediately.

contradicting.ticket: When a product media or category/collection is deleted, also delete its generated thumbnails and cached renditions.
contradicting.rule_test: Same static signal check: a new post_delete.connect / @receiver in saleor/product is a violation.

rules.neutral_patch: In saleor/graphql/account, wrap the two explicit pre-delete calls in a single helper function (~15 lines); no signal introduced.
rules.why: Cheaply greppable; natural contradicting site saleor/product (3 post_delete connects in apps.py, 0 explicit counterparts). Also existing breaks in account (apps.py:12), app (apps.py:13,18; app/tasks.py:82 follows), thumbnail (apps.py:12), schedulers/models.py:137-142 (4 connects). Weakness: 'follows' is hard to count objectively; the consistent site relies on a judgment call. Beware that the product/thumbnail cleanup handlers are legitimate legacy and agents will copy them.

rules.statement: Gift card balance changes must be a single atomic, race-safe operation (lock or DB-level expression, self-clamped at zero), never read-decide-write across separate steps, and balance adjustment is a dedicated operation, not an editable field on the general update.

signature.follows: select_for_update() (gift_card_qs_select_for_update() or .select_for_update().get()) held across read+write inside transaction, and/or F('current_balance_amount') +- amount. grep: 'select_for_update|F\("current_balance_amount"\)'
signature.breaks: reading current_balance_amount then writing it back unlocked, or putting current_balance_amount in cleaned_input of the generic create/update mutation. grep: 'current_balance_amount\s*[-+]?=|\["current_balance_amount"\]'

consistent.ticket: Add a goodwill 'topUp' operation that adds an amount to a gift card from a stored-value promotion.
consistent.rule_test: Run two concurrent top-ups/charges against one card (threads with real DB) or inspect the SQL: assert the final balance equals the sum of both effects and never goes below zero; no unlocked read-modify-write.

none.package: saleor/graphql/order (non-test; touches gift cards only via lines, no balance writes)
none.ticket: On order cancellation by staff, add an option to refund the amount paid by gift card back onto that card.
none.rule_test: Concurrent cancel-refund and checkout charge on the same card: final balance equals both effects; and no read-modify-write of current_balance_amount.

contradicting.ticket: Add a goodwill 'topUp' operation that adds an amount to a gift card from a stored-value promotion.
contradicting.rule_test: Same concurrency test through the new GraphQL mutation; plus assert balance is not changeable through giftCardUpdate-style generic input.
contradicting.seeding: Natural only under a loose reading: update.py:82 is a true break; create/bulk_create set the INITIAL balance of a new row (no race), so counting them is debatable. If a strict reader rejects them, seed by removing gift_card_qs_select_for_update() in gift_card_balance_adjust.py:88 (use the pre-loaded instance; ~3 lines) and adding a balance_amount write in one more mutation. Tests that would fail: saleor/graphql/giftcard/tests/mutations/test_gift_card_balance_adjust* (lock/concurrency assertions, if any).

rules.neutral_patch: In saleor/giftcard/gateway.py, extract the 'lock card then read balance' snippet used at lines 151/327/439 into one helper (~15 lines); locking and atomicity unchanged.
rules.why: Natural sites exist but precedent counting is judgment-heavy (lock-based vs F() vs create-time writes) and the violation is only visible to a concurrency test or SQL inspection, which a hidden test can do but is flaky-prone; verify the strict reading before running.
